description: Compute the electronic-energy reaction profile of thermal CO oxidation (CO + 1/2 O2 -> CO2) on the Pt(111) FCC surface via the Langmuir-Hinshelwood mechanism.
user_prompt: Compute the Langmuir-Hinshelwood reaction profile of thermal CO oxidation (CO + 1/2 O2 -> CO2) on the Pt(111) FCC surface (space group Fm-3m). The mechanism proceeds via separate CO and O adsorption from the gas phase followed by surface combination of *CO + *O to release gas-phase CO2. Use gas-phase electronic references, and build the adsorption and surface-combination steps as intermediate context. Report the overall electronic reaction energy delta_E_total (in eV) for CO(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> CO2(g).

references: NIST Chemistry WebBook, NIST Standard Reference Database 69
method.modeling: Use a Pt(111) slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 2x2x1 or larger surface cell; follow the Langmuir-Hinshelwood path through *CO, *O, and CO2(g), with triplet O2 as the gas reference.

key_parameters.magnetism: ISPIN=1 for Pt slabs; ISPIN=2 for triplet O2

method.rationale: Eichler and Hafner report the GGA gas-phase CO oxidation heat of reaction as 3.41 eV, written here in the exothermic reaction-energy convention as delta_E_total = -3.41 eV. For the closed Langmuir-Hinshelwood cycle, the Pt slab, *CO, and *O intermediates cancel, so the stepwise surface profile must telescope to this same gas-reference value. NIST gives the experimental thermochemical reaction energy near -2.93 eV; the more exothermic GGA value is retained because the benchmark metric follows the cited electronic DFT convention, with tolerance covering PW91/PBE and gas-reference differences.
